items.name: YFG Water Drop Splash [Flux]
items.description:
YFG Water Drop Splash: High-Speed Droplet Photography Effects

YFG Water Drop Splash is a LoRA designed to replicate the mesmerizing aesthetic of high-speed water drop photography. Expect crystal-clear splashes, fluid arcs, and watery shapes that can either stand alone or transform other subjects into water-formed silhouettes.

Key Features

  1. High-Speed Photography Look

    • Imitates the sharp, elegant motion-freeze of splash photography.

    • Captures minute fluid details, droplets, and ripple patterns with vivid clarity.

  2. Versatile Water Shapes

    • Can mold entire scenes or objects into liquid forms—“water shaped image of a real scene.”

    • Perfect for standalone splash shots, conceptual art, or watery illusions.

  3. Flexible Prompting & Strength

    • Use the phrase “in the shape and style of a yfg-dr0p water drop splash photo of X” to summon explicit splash imagery.

    • Strength from 0.25 to 1.10:

      • ~0.8 (CLIP & Model) is ideal for balanced clarity and watery detail.

      • Lower for subtle droplet accents; higher for dramatic, liquid-dominant transformations.

  4. Trigger Word

    • “YFG-Dr0p” helps direct the LoRA toward splash-based visuals and ensures watery aesthetics take center stage.

Recommended Usage

  • Prompt Suggestions

    • “In the shape and style of a yfg-dr0p water drop splash photo of a hummingbird”

    • “Crystal-clear water splash forming a human silhouette, YFG-Dr0p style”

    • “High-speed droplet collision above a reflective surface”

  • Combining With Other Themes

    • Pair with environment or object prompts to see them morphed into aquatic forms—like glass, ice, or clear water illusions.

Tips & Tricks

  1. Focus on Lighting & Reflection

    • High-speed water photography stands out with carefully chosen lighting and reflections.

    • Prompt ideas like “backlit droplets,” “shimmering highlights,” or “reflective surface” to accentuate watery realism.

  2. Experiment With Strength

    • For mild water details, keep the LoRA around 0.3–0.5.

    • For intense, all-encompassing droplets and splash shapes, push closer to 1.0 or even beyond.

  3. Create Liquid Sculpture Scenes

    • Prompt for swirling arcs, colliding droplets, or layered splashes.

    • Combine with negative prompts if you prefer less cluttered water shapes.

  4. Combine With Other LoRAs

    • Stack with style or environment LoRAs, adjusting strengths so that watery transformations don’t overshadow your main composition unless intended.

YFG Water Drop Splash adds a striking, fluid dimension to your imagery—freezing splashes mid-air and crafting ethereal water sculptures with ease. Perfect for those seeking the crisp, dynamic energy of high-speed droplet photography in their generative art!

items.name: Aether Splash - Wan 2.2 5b i2v LoRA
items.description:
Join my Discord for help, workflows and news of new LoRAs!

🎈 Aether Splash – Water Balloon Impact LoRA for Wan 2.2 5B (i2v)

Aether Splash is a custom LoRA trained for slow-motion splashes — a single water balloon bursting on the subject’s face with full liquid impact.
It was designed specifically for image-to-video (i2v) workflows using Wan 2.2 5B, and works best with clear portraits or close-up images of people.
Best results are on human subjects, but it may work on others too!

Thanks to @bblink787 and @masslevel for video contributions!

💦 Trigger Phrase
Use this exact prompt to trigger the effect:

water balloon bursting on face

🧠 How to Use (i2v)
Start with an image around 768px resolution (512–768px works well)
– Portrait or landscape format is fine
– Should feature a clearly visible subject, preferably a person
– Front-facing or 3/4 angle works best

Prompt using the trigger phrase above
– Keep prompt minimal
– The LoRA tells the model to animate a balloon hitting and bursting on the face

⚙️ Inference Settings
• Mode: image-to-video (i2v)
• Model: Wan 2.2 5B
• Resolution: around 768px (landscape or portrait)
• FPS: 24
• Steps: 20
• CFG: 5
• Clip length: 5 seconds (121 frames)

✅ Best Practices
• Use a clean, well-lit portrait or close-up image
• Avoid clutter — splash effect is strongest with clear subjects
• Don’t include water balloons in the image — the animation adds them

Trained using Ostris's AI Toolkit.

items.name: drowning
items.description:
I've created a Lora because there's a surprising lack of simple scenes depicting people drowning, and Stable diffusion's 'drowning' doesn't function as desired. The Lora is primarily based on images where only the upper body is emerging in a sea with waves.

However, during the operational check of the created Lora, I found that including prompts related to the lower body, like skirts or socks, results in images of standing by the sea rather than being in it. Hence, please exclude prompts related to the lower half of the body.

On the other hand, for one-piece costumes like in Tokyo Mew Mew, increasing the Lora's strength makes it easier to generate images with the lower body submerged in water. Conversely, reducing the strength will result in images of wandering in shallow waters rather than drowning.
